subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for all legacy ownerless persisted session rows?
rationale: Rejecting an explicitly foreign owner matches the existing security invariant, but denying all ownerless rows is a broader upgrade policy that can stop existing plugin workflows and needs owner intent and a recovery contract.

options.title: Fail closed with recovery
options.body: Reject ownerless rows and provide an operator or doctor remediation path plus upgrade proof.

options.title: Migrate proven ownership
options.body: Assign ownership only where authoritative historical data can establish it before runtime enforcement.

options.title: Defer ownerless behavior
options.body: Fix explicit foreign-owner rejection now and decide legacy ownerless rows in a separate owner-reviewed change.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with recovery
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows and provide an operator or doctor remediation path plus upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh has the clearest history on the session projection, accessor, and persisted-state migration boundary affected by this policy.
